summary: The post-rerun sync-main-health failure is explained by schema-invalid worker status READY in the live control snapshot, not by product CI. Current worker validation does not accept READY; the health-sync job materialized such records and then failed during sync/validate/render before publishing GREEN health.
evidence: Canonical CI run 31781938150 attempt 2 passed every step on exact main@af6a17aa7969d40e8b19f7e9d19fe93cc9b1d9a9.
Swarm Control Plane run 31783469998 then materialized live control successfully but failed its Apply canonical CI health and rebuild validation fence step; publishing GREEN health was skipped.

tools/swarm/swarmctl.py defines accepted worker statuses as WORKING, WAITING, REVIEWING, INTEGRATING, BLOCKED, IDLE, STOPPED plus legacy ACTIVE, CLAIMING, DONE; READY is absent and validate_worker rejects anything outside that set.

The materialized live state contained sol-20260814-k8m4v2q7 with status READY from 08:18 UTC, before the 08:20 health-sync snapshot. sol-20260814-z7c2m8q4 also registered with READY and has now self-corrected to canonical IDLE.
sol-20260814-k8m4v2q7 subsequently self-corrected to IDLE and records that the exact-main rerun recovered from transient Rokit HTTP 403.

metadata.recommendedNext: Do not change gameplay or product contracts. Normalize any remaining invalid READY worker registrations, then re-exercise health synchronization. Separately harden worker registration/protocol helpers so new workers begin in a canonical status (typically IDLE before claim, WORKING/REVIEWING/etc. after ownership) rather than introducing READY snapshots that poison control validation.
